breadcrumb: 41. Our Oregon (coalition of ~31 labor/community organizations and individuals, incl. SEIU Oregon, Oregon Labor Federation, OCPP)
tldr: Our Oregon, a coalition of ~31 labor and community organizations and state legislators (including SEIU Oregon, Oregon Labor Federation, Oregon Education Association), submitted a letter opposing the Prosperity Council's draft recommendations. They argue the recommendations prioritize corporate tax cuts and deregulation rather than benefiting working families, pointing to 40 years of failed trickle-down economics. They specifically oppose cutting top marginal income tax rates, streamlining the corporate activities tax that funds schools, reducing regulations by 20%, and proposing a sales tax (rejected 9 times). Instead, they advocate for investments in workforce pipelines, schools, and quality of life, emphasizing that care workers—healthcare, childcare, behavioral health—overwhelmingly women and people of color, should be economic priorities.

bullets.text: Since 1979, wages for the top 1% have grown nearly three times faster than wages for workers at the bottom
Intel received billions in property tax exemptions and direct funding; Nike received custom tax deal worth over $2 billion across 30 years, yet both subsequently laid off thousands of workers
Coalition opposes draft recommendations to cut Oregon's top marginal income tax rates in a year when Oregon's wealthiest residents recorded the highest incomes in state history
Coalition opposes streamlining of the corporate activities tax that funds children's schools
Coalition opposes cutting regulations by an arbitrary 20% without naming specific regulations
Coalition opposes a sales tax, noting Oregon voters have rejected it nine times
Oregon's fastest-growing jobs—healthcare, home care, childcare, behavioral health—are performed overwhelmingly by women and people of color but barely mentioned in the Council's work
Submission signed by approximately 31 organizations including SEIU Oregon, Oregon Labor Federation, and Oregon Education Association, plus individual signatories including state legislators
